title: Realizing the affine algebraic blowup helper as a fibrewise free sheaf locus
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $h\in R$ a nonzerodivisor, and $U=D(h)\subset S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be affine, flat and of finite presentation, with geometrically integral fibres, meaning integral after every field extension. Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module whose restriction to $X_U$ is of finite presentation. Fix $r\in\mathbf N$ and assume that for every $u\in U$, the stalk $\mathcal F_{\xi_u}$ at the generic point $\xi_u$ of the fibre is free of rank $r$ over $\mathcal O_{X,\xi_u}$. Then there is a finitely generated ideal $I\subset R$ with $V(I)=V(h)$ and an open $V\subset X\times_S\operatorname{Bl}_I(S)$ whose map to $\operatorname{Bl}_I(S)$ is surjective and on which the module strict transform of $\mathcal F$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus r}$. Blowups and strict transforms are as in [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform]; in particular this is a $U$-admissible blowup [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Schemes, morphism properties, quasi-coherent modules, finite type and finite presentation, relative module flatness, integral schemes, fibres, generic points and residue fields are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, final paragraph, realizing Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, on blowup charts.

proof.text: Since $S$ is affine and $f$ is affine, write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ by [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ flat over $R$, and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes $R\to B$ finitely presented. Put $N=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$. The counit in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) gives $\widetilde N\cong\mathcal F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a) on $X$ to see that $N$ is finite over $B$. The open $X_U=f^{-1}(D(h))$ is the principal open $D(h)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the image of $h$ (a prime of $B$ avoids it exactly when its contraction to $R$ does), and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0) it is an affine open of $X$ whose restriction map $B\to\mathcal O_X(D(h))$ is a localization at $h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], its section module is $N_h$ over $B_h$; applying the same affine criterion (b) to this affine open shows that $N_h$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, final paragraph: affine translation before invoking Tag 0810; Properties Tags 01PB/01PC.

proof.text: For $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and a field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the extended fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RK)$. Geometric integrality and [def-pc-integral-scheme] imply that this ring is a nonzero domain. In particular put $C_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}=\ker(B\to C_{\mathfrak p})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2), the fibre's generic point is its zero prime; the projection to $X$ sends it to $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ by the spectrum definition. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identifies the assumed free stalk with $N_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}\cong B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}^{\oplus r}$ whenever $h\notin\mathfrak p$. Every hypothesis of [lem-trf-affine-generic-rank-blowup] now holds. Choose its finitely generated ideal $I$ with $V(I)=V(h)$ and retain its conclusion for every $a\in I$ and every prime of $R[I/a]$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, hypotheses and conclusion; Tag 0811 final paragraph.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty finite generating list $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ of $I$, adding a zero generator if necessary. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] the opens $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $R_i=R[I/a_i]$, cover $T=\operatorname{Bl}_I(S)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Y_i=X\times_ST_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $B_i=B\otimes_RR_i$, cover $Y=X\times_ST$. The extended ideal on $R_i$ is $(a_i)$: each $x\in I$ equals $a_i(x/a_i)$ in the chart subring of $R[1/a_i]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], and $a_i\in I$. Consequently the exceptional inverse image on $Y_i$ is $V(a_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], the ordinary pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $Y_i$ is $\widetilde{P_i}$ for $P_i=N\otimes_RR_i$; here $B_i\otimes_BN\cong N\otimes_RR_i$ sends $(b\otimes c)\otimes n$ to $bn\otimes c$, with inverse $n\otimes c\mapsto(1\otimes c)\otimes n$.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 0806, lemma-universal-property-blowing-up; affine chart calculation in lemma-strict-transform (Tag 080E).

proof.text: On $Y_i$, the subsheaf removed in [def-trf-module-strict-transform] consists exactly of sections of $\widetilde{P_i}$ zero off $V(a_i)$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-trf-principal-support-quotient-exact] over the ring $B_i$, with its element $a_i$, to the sequence $0\to0\to P_i\xrightarrow{1}P_i\to0$. This sequence is short exact and every map $0/a_i^n0\to P_i/a_i^nP_i$ is injective, so all hypotheses hold. The result identifies the removed subsheaf with $\widetilde{\Gamma_{(a_i)}P_i}$ and the quotient with $\widetilde{Q_i}$, where $Q_i=P_i/\{m:\exists n\ge0,\ a_i^nm=0\}$. Hence the actual strict transform $\mathcal F^b$ restricted to $Y_i$ is $\widetilde{Q_i}$. This uses the sheaf quotient identification of the cited statement, not exactness of global sections for arbitrary sheaves.

source.place: Tag 080E, lemma-strict-transform, final affine-module paragraph; Tag 080W, lemma-strict-transform-universally-injective, principal-support quotient calculation.

proof.text: For every $\mathfrak p'\in\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, the algebraic helper gives $g\in B_i$ with nonzero image in $B_i\otimes_{R_i}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and $(Q_i)_g\cong(B_i)_g^{\oplus r}$. Let $W_{i,\mathfrak p'}=D(g)\subset Y_i$, an open by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. The localization description [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], together with [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module], gives $\mathcal F^b|_{W_{i,\mathfrak p'}}\cong\mathcal O_{W_{i,\mathfrak p'}}^{\oplus r}$. This open meets the fibre over $\mathfrak p'$: writing $\mathfrak p$ for its image in $S$, the field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and tensor associativity identify the fibre algebra with $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, a nonzero domain by geometric integrality as in Step 2. Its zero prime avoids the nonzero image of $g$, and its inverse image in $B_i$ is a point of $D(g)$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, conclusion; Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, final paragraph, fibrewise nonempty free opens.

proof.text: Set $V=\bigcup_{i,\mathfrak p'}W_{i,\mathfrak p'}\subset Y$. A union of opens is open. Every point of $T$ belongs to some $T_i$ and has a preimage in the corresponding $W_{i,\mathfrak p'}$, so $V\to T$ is surjective. The displayed free identifications on these opens prove the required local isomorphism on $V$; no compatibility between chosen bases is needed. Finally $V(I)=V(h)$ implies that the ideal sheaf associated to $I$ restricts to the unit ideal on $D(h)$: at each such prime some generator of $I$ is invertible. Its finite generators give local finite generation of that quasi-coherent ideal, and $D(h)$ is quasi-compact since it is affine. Thus $I$ with its blowup is a $U$-admissible datum by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup].

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, final paragraph; elementary union and admissibility check after applying Tag 0810.
